summary: Two admissible exact counterexamples invalidate central midpoint/equidistance guarantees; empirical damage is not inferred.

problems.claim: Angular spherical mean provides original-manifold geodesic equidistance
problems.location: p2 desideratum3; p5 midpoint statement; p6 Eq22; p17 Table5

assumptions.training_set: only u and v; both strictly opposite sides

problems.check: Boundary normal (1,-1,0)/sqrt2; shortest sphere distance arcsin absolute inner product
problems.result: Distances pi/4 approximately 0.785398 and asin(1/(2sqrt(2))) approximately 0.361367 differ.
problems.counterevidence: Equal projected radii would rescue pairwise equality, but unstated and not true in example; no angle-wrap/antipodal issue
problems.impact: Core five-desiderata guarantee fails; useful convex splits and empirical performance may survive

correction.statement: For unit-norm non-antipodal sphere points with nonzero projected sum, angle atan2(u0+v0,ud+vd) gives equal pairwise distances
correction.support: Normal annihilates u+v so absolute inner products equal
correction.limits: Pairwise property only; no full algorithm certification

problems.claim: Eqs. 20-21 define a hyperbolic midpoint candidate
problems.location: p5 Section 3.2 Eqs. 20-21; Algorithm 1 candidate rule
problems.check: V=-2coth1; cot<-1 cannot equal x1/x0=tanh t
problems.result: Boundary does not intersect manifold; correct midpoint parameter t=.5
problems.counterevidence: Both code snapshots use different (-V-sqrt(V^2-4))/2, correct for this example; no evidence printed formula generated experiments
problems.impact: Published explicit core construction invalid; no benchmark score damage claimed

correction.statement: For this pair correct cot is tanh(.5); source branch reproduces it
correction.limits: No full replacement certified; symmetric-input singularity needs separate handling
